quarterly_data.signal: Management's outlook (annual securities report): demand for generative-AI server substrates remains strong and general-purpose server demand keeps growing moderately; for FY2027 (the company's fiscal 2026, beginning April 2026) the company expects demand for high-performance IC package substrates as a whole, including those for general-purpose servers, to grow, as AI expands further and higher processing power must be combined with lower power consumption. The company will invest a total of approx. JPY 500 billion in the Electronics business over the three years FY2027 to FY2029 (the company's fiscal 2026 to 2028) to capture rising orders for high-value-added products in growth markets, and will strengthen quality globally under its One Factory concept.

quarterly_data.signal: Capital expenditure in the year ended March 2026 (annual securities report): JPY 64,277 million in total, mainly new equipment to expand production capacity (JPY 59,647 million at the parent company, centred on large Electronics investments). Electronics JPY 58,066 million, mainly package substrate manufacturing equipment; Ceramics JPY 1,758 million, mainly special carbon (FGM) and EV battery safety part production equipment; Other and corporate JPY 4,452 million. No retirement materially affecting production capacity. Management states capex to expand IC package substrate capacity continues in order to meet strong customer demand.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 64,277 million; Electronics JPY 58,066 million

quarterly_data.signal: Segment analysis, year ended March 2026 (annual securities report): in Electronics, management states orders for generative-AI server substrates were firm overall, PC demand came in below expectations, demand for high-performance IC package substrates for general-purpose servers recovered moderately, and cost-reduction activities at the Philippines plant helped. Ceramics net sales JPY 82,554 million (-1.8%), segment profit JPY 7,646 million (-37.4%): DPF sales and profit fell as lower production volume worsened manufacturing costs, AFP volumes fell, special carbon (FGM) fell on weak power-semiconductor demand hit by the EV slowdown and continued inventory adjustment at some customers, and EV battery safety parts (NEV) grew sales after mass production began but stayed loss-making as the EV market slowed more than expected. Other net sales JPY 90,330 million (+2.5%), segment profit JPY 8,964 million (+3.0%). Against the plan set at the start of the year, operating income of JPY 62,027 million beat the JPY 48,000 million plan. Outlook: in FGM the company plans investment to expand beyond semiconductor manufacturing equipment into the energy (nuclear power) field, and will push orders for EV battery safety and peripheral parts.
quarterly_data.figure: Ceramics sales JPY 82,554 million (-1.8%), profit JPY 7,646 million (-37.4%); operating income JPY 62,027 million vs JPY 48,000 million plan

quarterly_data.signal: Impairment (annual securities report): Ibiden Philippines' fixed assets were impaired by JPY 10,630 million in the year ended March 2026 (JPY 15,537 million a year earlier) because PC substrate demand recovery lacked strength and price competition among suppliers intensified, worsening expected cash flows; total impairment losses for the year were JPY 16,405 million (Electronics JPY 13,873 million, Ceramics JPY 2,024 million), against JPY 18,587 million a year earlier.
quarterly_data.figure: Philippines impairment JPY 10,630 million; total impairment JPY 16,405 million

quarterly_data.signal: R&D (annual securities report): group R&D spending JPY 29,916 million in the year ended March 2026, of which Electronics JPY 26,918 million - product design, element technologies and process technologies for IoT, 5G communications, AI, data centers and automotive, developing high-density, high-performance package substrates for high-speed transmission and low loss; Ceramics JPY 2,830 million - parts for NEV safety, semiconductor-related parts and high-performance exhaust systems.
